runtimeEnforcement.approvedReferencePngDigests: Runtime-enforced by auth-d1-visual.spec.ts (beforeAll) and test/auth.d1-visual-references.test.ts for all 20 exports.
runtimeEnforcement.derivedBaselineDigests: Pixel-compared frames: each baseline is re-derived from its export (status bar removed) and compared byte for byte before and after every screenshot, so --update-snapshots can never overwrite one silently.
runtimeEnforcement.perFrameAllowance: maxDiffPixelRatio per screenshot, read by the spec from this manifest.

sourceDesign.provenanceNote: Twenty D1 frames (invitation confirmation, claim password, claim verify; light and dark) exported read-only at scale 1 (390x844) and committed unchanged. They were designed after D1 left these surfaces blocked in docs/design/clubhouse-approval-matrix.md and approved by the issue owner.

comparison.viewport: 390×800 CSS px, deviceScaleFactor 1, viewport screenshot. The pen frame is 390×844: its top 44px is the OS status bar the app never renders, so the baseline is the export with exactly those rows removed (deriveCroppedTopPng).
comparison.environment: Chromium with the playwright.config.ts deterministic raster flags, service worker blocked, reduced motion, Figtree 400-800 loaded before capture. Dark frames use the theme=dark cookie.
comparison.structuralProbes: Exact geometry (±1px, bar ±2px): top bar 56px with centered 17px title; 56×56 tile at x20 y72 radius 12; 52px controls at x20 width 350; sticky action bar 12/20/24 inset with 1px hairline top border; four 4px strength segments; no text-transform; 320px and 1280px control fit with ≥44px targets.

calibration.environment: macOS (Darwin), Playwright Chromium, pnpm test:e2e e2e/auth-d1-visual.spec.ts with every allowance 0 so each nonzero residual is reported by the comparator
calibration.allowancePolicy: Measured ratio rounded up to 0.05pp, plus 0.25pp headroom for Pencil-vs-Chromium rasterization drift across OS (Linux CI measurement not available locally). Geometry probes stay exact and are never widened.
calibration.justification: Residual is dominated by documented, intentional divergences (knownDivergences) plus text antialiasing and half-pixel placement. Structure is gated by the geometry probes, not by the pixel budget. The Figtree typeface and Clubhouse chrome come from the U2/U3 units.

invite-default: Frame b7ymtm reads "Invitation accepted / Continue to sign in": it shows a completed acceptance. The real default is the pre-acceptance confirmation (one-use POST), so the real copy (Confirm your invitation, Accept invitation) is kept; no state is shown as accepted before the POST.

The app keeps its secondary "Cancel and keep current account" action (and the account-switch warning when a session exists), so the sticky bar is 148px instead of 88px: that 60px strip plus the shifted accept button is most of the residual.
The frame draws a back chevron; there is no safe back destination (no invented exit), so only the title is drawn, as in the U6 auth frames.
invite-expired: Frame text differs from the real, truthful copy (confirmation unavailable, open the original invitation again).
"Contact support" opens a mailto link to the existing privacy contact address; the app has no dedicated support route.
invite-busy: The frame loader icon is static here (no spinner animation under reduced motion); the real POST navigates away, so the busy screen is transient.
claim-password: The frame draws disabled Continue (surface-2 button) until both rules pass and an eye (show password) control on each field. The app keeps submit-time validation (behavior preserved: no live-disabled submit, no show-password toggle), so the button is the enabled primary CTA labelled "Save password" and the eye controls are absent; the 52px button strip is about 5.8pp of the residual.
Rule 1 is the real policy copy (D2 truthful) and wraps to two lines; the frame shows "At least 10 characters" on one line.
Labels use the shared copy ("Repeat password"); the frame says "Confirm password".
The first field is drawn focused in the frame; the app focuses the heading on mount (screen-reader announcement, unchanged behavior).
claim-password-strong: Same label/placeholder/policy-copy differences as the empty state; the button matches (enabled primary).
claim-password-error: The frame pairs the mismatch error with strength Fair; the app only reports a mismatch after the policy passed, so the same state shows strength Strong with rule 1 met and rule 2 unmet. Disabled Continue and eye controls as in the empty state.
claim-verify: No pixel comparison: the frame draws a six-digit code entry, "Resend code" and a "Verify email" button. The app has no code entry (verification is an emailed recovery link). The implemented screen keeps the chip, heading, options card and sticky "Email me a link" action in the frame structure. Requires no behavior change; not invented.
